liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (1 review): Weir’s jamming is highlighted, though the recording is unfortunately cut in the middle [5]
- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): Playin' In The Band is cited as one of the best versions ever recorded [10]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Early version lacks the 'gonna make 'em Shine' lyric, instead using 'Can't keep from cryyyyyyin'; Jerry's voice shines on this gorgeous version, making it worth listening for alone [11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The band pulls off an extraordinary China Cat Sunflower and I Know You Rider transition [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd72-12-10 t01 Bertha**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t02 Playin' In The Band**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t03 Casey Jones**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t04 Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t05 Promised Land**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t06 Stella Blue**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t07 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **gd72-12-10 t08 China Cat Sunflower**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-12-10.141755.sbd.s1ps2.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 18 songs; 137 min [1]
- **gd72-12-10.sbd.gorinsky.5801.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 143 min; rated 3.75/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording features hiss and level issues, but captures excellent performance of this song; Truckin' is described as bouncy, though the audio is noted as being trusted down; Soundboard is imperfect, and the Other One suffers from a devastating cut in the middle [5][10][13]
- **gd1972-12-10.132778.sbd.droncit.restore5801.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 144 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Coldest night of the year; band waited on Post Street before starting with this song [7]
- New Riders likely opened, but delay caused Dead to start immediately without the opener [7]
- Performance at Winterland Arena described as spectacular, with Playin' In The Band being cosmic [8]
- Four inches of snow fell 25 miles east; rare and unusual for the San Francisco Bay Area [9]
- Stairway to Heaven had recently been released, prompting discussion among attendees on the way to the gig [9]
- Billy's drumming is fine, but the master tape has weird and apparently live mixing [13]
- Most of Set One is missing, including Cold Rain & Snow and Black Throated Wind [1]
- Described as a bookend to the unusual July 25, 1972 version of the song [6]
- Truckin' has a 1972 bounce and invokes the September 28, 1972 Stanley Theatre version [8]
- This late 1972 show is similar to others but distinguished by an all-time Other One [14]
- Playin' In The Band is an epic, comparable to versions from November 18 and October 26 [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-12-10.141755.sbd.s1ps2.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Partial Show Source Info: Master Soundboard Reels > 2 cassette generations > Dat (16-bit/48k); Transfer Info: Dat (Sony PCM-R500) (16-bit/48k)>… [1]
- **gd72-12-10.sbd.gorinsky.5801.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]
- **gd1972-12-10.132778.sbd.droncit.restore5801.flac16**: transferred by droncit; source: Restored version of source ID 5801 (MSR > Cass x 3 > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN) by Droncit; Diamond Cut 8.5 Forensics was used for equalization and virtual valve… [3]
